chapters.title: Safety rules and the NO-GO list

blocks.text: People first, trailer second. If something here conflicts with a label on the trailer or an appliance manual, follow the label or the manual.
If you smell propane (Manual)
Put out every flame, pilot light and cigarette.
Get everyone out of the trailer.
Shut the cylinder valves, if you can reach them safely.
Don't touch any switch, phone or radio inside. Don't start an engine or generator.
Open doors and vents from outside if it's safe, and stay away until the smell clears.
Call a propane supplier, an RV technician or the fire department.
Keep the gas off until the leak is found and fixed.
Alarms and fire gear (Manual)

The 2019 Venture family manual describes SAFE-T-ALERT LP/CO alarm variants. Check the exact model and replacement date on your installed detector; its label controls service life, power source and test sequence. Do not assume a factory manual example identifies your installed unit.

The general 2019 manual describes a battery-operated smoke alarm, but use the installed alarm label for battery type, end-of-life date and test interval. Test after storage and before occupancy; replace any expired or nonfunctional unit.
Locate the installed fire extinguisher near the entry, check its rating, gauge, inspection tag and accessibility. Replace or service as its label requires.
Write the install date on each alarm, and replace it on time.
Rules Venture states outright (Manual)
Never use the range or oven to heat the trailer. Open a vent or window whenever you cook.
Never run a portable grill, heater or charcoal burner inside.
Never plug the trailer into a household outlet, use a cheater plug, or remove a ground pin.
Never fit a fuse or breaker rated higher than the one it replaces.
Turn off every pilot, appliance and igniter before refueling the tow vehicle or filling propane.
Don't run the furnace while towing.
Never fire the water heater, on gas or electric, without water in it.
Block the wheels before unhitching. Stabilizer jacks steady the trailer. They don't hold its weight.
The rear bumper carries 100 lb. Only the spare tire carrier belongs on it. The frame isn't built to tow anything.
The trailer isn't a four-season unit or a full-time home. Freeze damage isn't covered by Venture's warranty.
Common sense not in the manual (General)
No passengers in the trailer while it's moving.
Retract the awning in wind, in rain and whenever you leave the site.
Keep people and pets clear of slide paths, jacks and the hitch while anything moves.
NO-GO list. Don't tow until it's fixed.

By Venture's own formula, this trailer has about 893 lb for cargo once its water and propane are full. That's tight for a bunkhouse, so weigh it loaded at least once.
Venture's cargo formula (Manual)
Cargo carrying capacity is the GVWR minus the UVW, minus full fresh water (tank and water heater), minus full propane. Water weighs 8.3 lb per gallon in Venture's figures.

blocks.text: Two cautions. The UVW is a rolling average, so your trailer's real figure may be higher or lower. And the manual's general tire section says full propane counts as part of the trailer's own weight, which would make the figure 953 lb. The cargo sticker inside your trailer settles both, so use its number over this one.

Everything you carry comes out of that figure: food, clothes, bedding, tools, the house battery, outdoor kitchen gear, bikes and anything on a cargo tray. Driving with the fresh tank empty frees 332 lb.

blocks.text: Weighing the trailer (Manual)
Use a truck scale, loaded the way you travel.
Pull on so the trailer's tires and tongue jack sit 12 to 24 in in from the scale edge.
Lower the tongue jack, unhitch, and pull the tow vehicle forward 6 to 8 in so none of it is on the scale. Record the weight. That's the whole trailer.
Re-hitch. Make sure no part of the tow vehicle is on the scale. Record the weight. That's the trailer axles only.
Subtract the axle weight from the whole-trailer weight. The difference is your hitch weight.
Weigh each side of the axles separately too. Venture notes the slide side or fridge side often runs heavier, and one side can be over while the other is fine.

rows: Hitch and receiver rating, truck payload
Load rating of those two tires
Load rating of those two tires
Truck GVWR and rear axle rating

blocks.text: Every row has to pass. If one fails, take weight out or move it. Don't plan around hope.
Loading rules
Load two pounds ahead of the axles for every pound behind them. Weight behind the axles lightens the hitch and makes sway worse. (Manual)
Heavy items low and near the axles, light bulky items in overhead cabinets. Secure anything that can slide. (Manual)
Keep the rear bumper to the spare carrier only, 100 lb. The ladder takes 200 lb, and you can't carry cargo on it. (Manual)
An optional flip-down cargo tray is rated 250 lb, including a spare tire if one is mounted on it. Your spare is undermount on the 2019 Touring. (Manual, 2019 spec)
Venture's dry hitch weight is about 12 percent of its dry weight. Many hitch makers want 10 to 15 percent of loaded weight on the hitch, but your hitch and tow vehicle ratings come first. (General)

chapters.title: Towing, hitching, tires, wheels and brakes

blocks.text: Match the tow vehicle to the loaded trailer, set the hitch height right, and keep tires at cold pressure. Those three prevent most towing trouble.
Tow vehicle and hitch (Manual)
Check the tow vehicle's GVWR and GCWR against your scale numbers from the Load and Weight Worksheet. A longer wheelbase tows better.
Have a hitch shop fit a weight-distributing hitch, with sway control if your rig needs it. A wrong-size hitch can damage the trailer frame or the tow vehicle.
With the trailer level on flat ground, the inside of the coupler socket sits about 18 to 22 in off the ground. Add 1 to 2 in to the ball height to allow for tow vehicle sag.
Tandem axles should ride level, so both axles carry similar weight.
Hooking up (Manual, adapted to the power tongue jack)
Chock the trailer wheels. Raise the tongue with the power jack until the coupler clears the ball.
Open the coupler latch and back the tow vehicle into place.
Lower the coupler fully onto the ball, then close and pin the latch.
Fit the weight-distributing bars as the hitch maker specifies.
Raise the tongue jack all the way.
Clip the breakaway cable to the tow vehicle, not to the safety chains.
Cross the safety chains under the coupler: left chain to the right receiver loop, right chain to the left.
Plug in the 7-way connector.
Check every exterior light, stabilizers up, steps in, fridge door latched, loose items secured.
Test the trailer brakes before you enter the road.
Tires (Manual)
Check pressure cold before each trip and at least weekly during use. A tire is cold after sitting three hours or more, whatever the weather.

The placard pressure is for full load. Venture says you may run slightly lower with a light load, but never above the sidewall limit and never below what your scale weights call for in the tire maker's load table.
Venture's original tires carry a speed rating of 75 mph or more. Read the actual rating and load limit on your sidewalls.
Since 2017, Venture fills tires with nitrogen. Green valve caps mark them.
Replace at 1/16 in of tread, or sooner if the wear bars show. Replace with the same size and load range.
A tread puncture can be plugged and patched from inside. A sidewall puncture can't be repaired.
Tires aren't balanced from the factory. Alignment after pothole damage is a shop job and isn't covered by warranty.
Replace tires on age as well as tread. Check the DOT date code on each sidewall. (General)
Wheels and lug nuts (Manual)

rows: 90 to 120 ft-lb, or the wheel decal if it says otherwise
At 50 and 200 miles after any wheel goes on, then every 500 miles
After storage, before each trip, after hard braking
150 ft-lb. The nut or the wheel seat fails.
13/16 in standard nut, 3/4 in chrome nut

blocks.text: Powder-coated wheels can take several passes to hold torque because of the paint.
Wheel bearings (Manual, 2019 spec)

Your trailer has E-Z Lube hubs. The 2019 general owner manual mentions adding grease when needed, but the correct method and quantity must follow the identification plate and installed axle manufacturer's instructions. Excessive grease can reach brakes. Have bearings and seals inspected and serviced to the axle maker's intervals. (2019 Venture features; axle maker required)
Electric brakes (Manual)
The brakes need a brake controller in the tow vehicle, powered by the tow vehicle's battery. Keep that battery and charging system healthy.
Brakes are 10 or 12 in electric, wired in parallel with 14-gauge wire.
They self-adjust as you tow forward and back.
Use the foot pedal for normal braking. Save the controller's manual lever for slow movement or icy roads.
Start braking gently on wet roads. On long grades, drop a gear early so the brakes don't overheat.
Breakaway switch (Manual)
If the trailer separates, the pin pulls out and the switch powers the trailer brakes from the house battery.
It needs a battery at least as strong as a 12 V, 12 Ah wet-cell. No battery, no breakaway brakes.
Never use it as a parking brake. It draws current constantly and can damage the wiring and switch.
Don't leave the pin out in storage. The contacts corrode.
On the road (Manual)
Expect slower acceleration, longer stops and wider turns. Leave more room to pass. Watch the mirrors often, brace for the push of air from passing trucks and buses, and slow down on wet roads.
Level first, then stabilize, then connect, then open the slides. The fridge, the drains and the slide seals all depend on a level trailer.
Pick and level the site
Walk the site. Look for soft ground, slope, low branches and wires, and room for all three slides and the 20 ft awning. (General)
Pull in, then chock the wheels before you unhitch. (Manual)
Level side to side first, while still hitched. Venture suggests short 2 x 6 in boards under the low-side wheels. The LevelMatePRO app shows how much height each side needs. (Manual, 2019 spec)
Put a block or pad under the tongue jack foot unless you're on concrete, so it doesn't sink. (Manual)
Unhitch (Manual)
Release the weight-distributing bars.
Open the coupler latch.
Raise the tongue with the power jack until the ball is free.
Disconnect the 7-way plug, the safety chains and the breakaway cable.
Raise the tongue a little more, then drive the tow vehicle away.
Level front to back with the tongue jack.
Lower the four stabilizer jacks until each makes firm contact with the ground or a pad.

Your stabilizers are BAL electric jacks with their own motors (2019 spec). They steady the trailer. They aren't built to lift it or level it, whatever the motor can do. Their breakers sit under the black cover by the battery disconnect on the front frame. (Manual)
Connect services, in this order
Power. Check the pedestal with a plug-in tester. Breaker off, plug in, breaker on. Use the 50 amp outlet, not an adapter, if you can. Details in the Electrical System chapter.

Water. Fit a 45 psi regulator at the hose bib, then a drinking-water hose. Open the faucets inside to purge air. The water heater fills first. Details in the Fresh Water, Water Heater and Plumbing chapter. (Manual)
Sewer. Connect and clamp the hose. Keep the black valve closed until the tank is at least 3/4 full. Details in the Toilets, Holding Tanks and Dumping chapter. (Manual)

Propane. Make sure all burners and controls are off. Open each cylinder valve slowly and listen. A hiss lasting more than a second or two means close it and look for a leak. Light a stove burner to bleed air from the lines. Details in the Propane System chapter. (Manual)
Slides. Only once the trailer is level and the stabilizers are firmly down. Clear the path inside and out. Details in the Slide-Outs chapter. (Manual)
Awning. Only in calm weather, and only while someone's around. (General)
Alarms. Test the smoke alarm and the CO and propane alarm. (Manual)
Open windows and roof vents for air if you like. Close them before you leave, since a raised vent can be torn off on the road. (Manual)
Departure
Run setup in reverse. Venture's pre-departure list (Manual):
Coupler pin or locking lever seated.
Breakaway cable attached to the tow vehicle.
All jacks raised clear of the ground.
Shore power cord stored.
Safety chains attached to the receiver.
Interior lights off.
Campfire out.

Also check that all three slides are fully in, the awning is stowed, the steps are up, roof vents and windows are shut, the fridge door is latched, propane valves are closed for travel, and the chocks are packed. The departure workbook in the Trip Workbooks chapter covers it line by line.
Your trailer has three slides, and Venture used more than one slide system across its 2019 trailers. Find out which system each slide uses before you ever reach for the manual override.
What Venture says it fits

The 2019 Touring construction page lists a rack-and-pinion electric slide with manual override and a box-tube ram, and triple-sealed slideouts (2019 spec). The owner's manual describes three systems Venture uses across its models (Manual):

rows: Steel rams and a cog track under the floor, a cross shaft front to rear, the motor in or on the main frame rail, all inside the underbelly
A 1/2 in shaft through the main frame rail with a 3/4 in nut. Use a 3/4 in socket, extension and ratchet. On some units the stabilizer crank handle fits.
A ram and cog track inside the trailer, under the slide floor, sofa or dinette. Large slides use two rams joined by a cross shaft.
Reach the ram from the front, under the slide floor, sofa or dinette. Lippert's version takes a 5/8 in socket, ratchet and usually an extension.
Four tracks on the slide's outer walls, two low and two near the roof, with a motor at the top of each side column, reached from inside
Use the Schwintec manual. It covers manual operation and error codes.

blocks.text: Power (Manual)
Slides run on 12 V from the converter or the house battery. The battery isn't supplied by Venture.
A 30 amp automatic-reset breaker in the load center protects the slides.
With a weak battery, plug in shore power or run the tow vehicle's 12 V feed to help the motor.
A slide takes about 20 seconds to move in or out.
Before you move a slide (Manual)
Level the trailer front to back and side to side.
Lower all four stabilizers to firm contact. That keeps the body square so the room seals.
Check that nothing blocks the room inside or out, and that people and pets are clear.
Stay away from the slide rails under the trailer while the room moves.
Running it (Manual)

The switch has three positions: off in the center, in and out. Hold it until the room seats and the gasket is slightly compressed, then let go. Holding it longer bends the outer flange or the inside fascia. Venture doesn't call for blocks or jacks under the slides during normal use.
Using the manual override
Level the trailer and lower the stabilizers. (Manual)
Switch off the slide breaker so nothing starts while you work. (General)
Clear the path and keep people away. (Manual)
Fit the socket for your system and turn steadily. Count turns so you'll feel a bind early. (General)
Stop when the room seats against its seal. (Manual)
Find and fix the power or mechanical fault before you use the switch again. (General)
Care (Manual, General)
Keep tracks clean. Venture stresses this for in-wall slides especially. In dusty or sandy places, check after every trip.
Wipe the bulb and wiper seals with mild soap and water, dry them, and treat them with a rubber conditioner made for RV seals. No petroleum products. (General)
Lubricate only with what the slide maker specifies. Grease on a rack picks up grit. (General)
Clear the gutters above the slides so water runs off. (2019 spec)
Venture uses flexible water and drain hoses where plumbing runs into a slide. If any of your slides carry them, check they aren't kinked or pinched. (Manual)
When a slide misbehaves

rows: Battery disconnect off, flat battery, tripped breaker, switch fault
Check the disconnect, battery, slide breaker and fuses.
Plug in shore power. Look for an obstruction.
Stripped gear, loose coupler, broken shaft
Stop. Bring it in with the override and book a repair.
Low voltage, dirty tracks, dragging seals, not level
One end moves ahead of the other
Stop. Don't force it. That needs the slide maker's procedure or a technician.
Won't seal, or leaks at a corner
Not level, worn seal, bent fascia, wrong stop
Relevel and check the seal. Leave stop adjustment to a technician.

blocks.text: What you shouldn't adjust yourself

Cleaning, seal care, tightening loose screws and clearing obstructions are owner jobs. Travel stops, ram alignment, cross-shaft timing and in-wall track sync aren't, unless you have the slide maker's service manual. A wrong setting bends the room or tears the seal.
Slide register (Check unit)
The locations follow Venture's 2019 floorplan. Confirm them on your trailer.

chapters.title: Fresh water, water heater and plumbing

blocks.text: Water reaches the faucets two ways: through the city inlet with a 45 psi regulator, or from the 40 gal tank through the 12 V pump. Make sure the 6 gal water heater is full before you switch it on.
plumbing layout · 40 gal fresh in, 64 gal gray and black out
This is a functional map, not a pipe route. Venture's manual shows two fill layouts, and which one you have depends on the floorplan, so find your valves before you rely on the V labels. (Check unit)
Which fill layout you have (Manual)

rows: Outside gravity fill. The overflow sits at 10 o'clock on the fill and spits water when full.
V1 opens the siphon hose only. V2 opens the tank to the pump, and stays closed while the siphon is in use.
No gravity fill. Three valves and a siphon hose in a cabinet near the pump.
V1 siphon hose. V2 tank to pump. V3 lets city water fill the tank. Close V3 when the tank's full.

blocks.text: Never leave the tank filling unattended. It isn't built to hold pressure, and an overfilled tank can crack or bend its carrier, which Venture doesn't treat as a defect. Watch the monitor panel while you fill. (Manual)
City water (Manual)
Fit a 45 psi regulator, then connect and open the supply. Open every faucet inside to let the air out. The water heater fills first, so expect some spitting before it runs steady.
12 V pump (Manual)
Turn it on at the monitor panel. It self-primes and runs until pressure reaches about 40 to 45 psi, then restarts at about 20 psi.
A built-in check valve stops water flowing back into the tank.
Clean the strainer cup on the inlet side at least once a year.

Short on-off bursts usually mean a faucet is slightly open or a water-saver washer is restricting flow. If it cycles every 10 to 15 minutes with everything shut, look for a small leak, a bad check valve in the city inlet, or the pump's own pressure valve.
Switch it off when you're not using it.
Things that look like leaks but aren't (Manual)
The bathroom shower head doesn't shut off fully and drips slightly.
The outside shower's vacuum breaker drains the hose after use.
Sanitize when new, after storage, or any time the water may be contaminated (Manual)
Mix 1/4 cup of household bleach (5 percent) per gallon of water. Make one gallon of that for every 15 gallons of tank, so about 2.7 gallons for your 40 gal tank.
Close all drains and set the water heater bypass so the heater is out of the system.
Draw the solution into the lines through the siphon hose (open V1, run the pump) until it comes out of every faucet.
To treat the tank, add solution through the gravity fill (System 1) or open V3 (System 2), then top up with water.
Run the solution through all faucets again, then let it stand three hours.
Drain and flush with fresh water.
If it tastes of chlorine, run 1 quart of vinegar per 5 gallons of water through the same way, leave 24 hours, then drain and flush.
Close V1 and open V2 for normal use.
Draining the system (Manual)
Open all faucets, including the outside shower.
Open the fresh tank drain under the floor.
Open the water heater drain.
Open all low-point drains. There are two to four, and they should drain to the ground, not into the underbelly.
Hold the toilet valve open.
Run the pump up to 20 seconds to empty it.
Water heater (2019 spec, Manual)

Yours is a 6 gallon gas/electric tank heater with direct spark ignition. The manual's water heater section refers you to a Suburban service center, so expect a Suburban unit. Confirm on the data plate behind the outside door.
Fill it first. Set both bypass valves horizontal (normal flow) and open a hot faucet until water runs steady with no air. Running it dry warps the tank and burns out the electric element.

On gas: Turn on propane and power, then flip the Gas switch on the monitor panel. The burner lights itself. It makes up to three tries, each after a 15 second purge, then locks out. To reset, switch off, wait five seconds, switch on. The first start after a refill may take several cycles.
On electric: The switch behind the outside door, lower left of the control housing, has to be on. Then flip the Electric switch on the monitor panel.
Don't run gas and electric together. (Manual caution)
Don't run it on gas if an open exterior door could block its vent.
If it won't light, check the switch, the propane supply and the ECO reset button. Then call a service center.
If any part has been under water, don't use it until a technician has inspected it.
Turn the propane off while traveling or when the trailer isn't in use.

Suburban tank heaters have a steel tank with an anode rod that wears away and needs checking each year. (General) Venture's manual says that if you winterize without the bypass, take the anode out and fit a 3/4 in drain plug for the winter.
Your fresh tank compartment has holes into the floor heat duct, so the furnace warms it. The holding tanks may not be heated. (Manual)
Use plenty of water, keep the black valve closed until the tank is at least 3/4 full, and always dump black before gray.
Toilets (Manual, 2019 spec)

The floorplan shows two toilets, one in the main bath and one in the rear half bath. Venture lists a porcelain toilet, and the manual names the Thetford Aqua Magic Residence with a foot pedal. Confirm the model on each toilet. (Check unit)
Press the pedal all the way down to flush. Press it halfway to add water.
Keep 4 to 6 in of water in the bowl while camping. About 2 in is fine for travel.
Let water run 10 to 20 seconds after each flush. An RV toilet uses 2 to 3 quarts a flush, and too little water leaves waste in the pipe, where it clogs.
Before first use and after every dump, put 2 quarts of water and the recommended dose of holding-tank chemical in the bowl, then flush it down with up to 2 gallons of water.
Tanks, vents and traps (Manual)
The gray tank (64 gal) takes the sinks, tub and shower. The black tank (64 gal) takes the toilets.
Vent pipes run from the tanks to the roof and let air out so waste can drain in. Some floorplans vent the gray tank through a louvered side vent instead.
Every drain has a P-trap. Water sloshes out of traps on the road, which is why the trailer can smell after a drive. Run water into each drain when you arrive.
Baking soda or a tank deodorizer in the gray tank cuts food odors.
At a full-hookup site (Manual)
Keep the black termination valve closed until the tank is at least 3/4 full, so there's enough liquid to carry the solids out. A closed valve also keeps sewer gas out of the trailer.
Dumping (Manual)
Park as level as you can. Some tanks drain from the center and some from an end, which changes the best tilt.
Remove the cap, fit the adapter and twist it about 10 degrees to lock on its pegs.
Clamp the sewer hose to the adapter and put the other end into the sewer.
Open the 3 in black valve first. Let it empty completely.
Close it, then open the gray valve to rinse the hose and lines.
Close both valves, rinse and stow the hose, cap the outlet.
Dump only at a proper station or sewer connection. Most places make anything else illegal.
Black tank flush (2019 spec, Manual)
The flush is standard on your trailer. It rinses the black tank after it's been emptied.
Open the termination valves first. Never run the flush with the black valve closed, or the tank fills with flush water.
Connect a hose to the inlet marked Sewer Tank Flusher.
Open the supply and rinse for several minutes.
Close the supply and disconnect.
Use a separate hose for flushing and never use it for drinking water. Stay with the hose while it runs. (General)
After a flush, the tank sensors may still read partly full because they're wet. Let them dry. (Manual)
Keeping the tanks clean

Venture's manual passes on the tank supplier's advice. For the gray tank, put 8 to 10 gallons of warm water and a degreaser such as dish soap in the tank before a drive, then drain and rinse. For the black tank, it suggests 8 to 10 gallons of water and a bottle of household drain cleaner, left in while traveling, then drained and rinsed.

Conflict between sources: the uploaded PDF warns against household drain openers and caustic chemicals in the waste system, and many valve and seal makers say the same. Venture's manual says the opposite for the black tank. Until your termination valve maker or Thetford approves it, I'd use a cleaner sold for RV holding tanks instead of a household drain cleaner. Never mix chemicals.
Odor or slow drains

rows: Toilet bowl water, dry P-traps, black valve left open at a hookup, a blocked roof vent
Not enough water per flush, solids pyramid under the toilet. Add water, flush the tank.
Wet or fouled probes. Flush and clean the tank.
Leak under a toilet or at a tank fitting
Turn the water off and book a repair. (Pro only)

blocks.text: Two 30 lb cylinders feed an automatic changeover regulator set to 11 in water column. Open valves slowly, leak-test every year, and never fill past 80 percent.
Cylinders (2019 spec, Manual)
Two 30 lb DOT cylinders sit on the tongue under a flip-up cover, 60 lb in all.
Each has an OPD valve. Open and close it by hand only. Tools damage it.
The small screw on the side is the 10 percent valve. Fillers use it to see the 80 percent mark. A float inside also stops the fill at 80 percent.
Pressure in a cylinder rises about 1.5 percent for every 10 degrees F of temperature rise. A cylinder filled cold and then parked in the sun can reach the point where its relief valve vents.

A strong smell around the cylinders on a hot day can mean an overfilled cylinder venting. Keep flames away. Venture's manual describes burning off the excess at a safe distance. I'd take it to a propane supplier instead.
Only a trained filler should fill or purge a cylinder.
Never store or carry cylinders inside the trailer or the tow vehicle cab.
Fit the dust cap whenever a cylinder is disconnected, and keep a loose cylinder from rolling around in transport.
Removing and refitting a cylinder (Manual)
Close the cylinder valve first, so no air gets in.
The ACME connector has a left-hand thread. Turn it clockwise to loosen.
After filling, reconnect by turning counterclockwise, snug but not overtight.
Reinstall the hold-down rod, bracket and wing nut.
Open the valve slowly and leak-test the connection.
Regulator (Manual)
It's an automatic two-stage regulator. The first stage drops cylinder pressure to 10 to 13 psi, and the second stage drops it to 11 in water column for the appliances.
Turn the lever toward the cylinder you want to use first. That one becomes supply and the other reserve.
When the supply cylinder runs down to about 10 psi, the reserve takes over and a red flag shows in the window. Swap the empty cylinder then.
The vent must face down and stay uncovered, or the regulator can't work.
The setting should be 11 in water column, plus or minus 1/2 in. Have a technician check it with a manometer once a year. (Pro only)
Hoses and the flow limiter (Manual)

The hose from each cylinder has a flow-limiting device. If you open a valve too fast it can trip and stop the flow, which feels like a frozen regulator. Close the valve, wait 15 minutes, then open it slowly. It also limits flow if a line ruptures. Turn off every pilot so pressure can equalize.
Turning the gas on (Manual)
Check that every burner, control and pilot valve is off.
Open each cylinder valve slowly.
Listen. A hiss lasting more than one or two seconds means close the valve and look for a leak.
Light the appliances as their instructions say. Expect a delay at the stove after a refill while air clears the line.
Keep the cylinder valves closed while you travel. Some places, including some tunnels, ban open valves on the road. (Manual)
Leak checks (Manual)
Test the whole system at least once a year, and after any fitting is moved or a cylinder is swapped.
Use soapy water or a bubble solution with no ammonia or chlorine. Bubbles mean a leak. Never use a flame.
Tighten brass fittings with two open-end wrenches, so you don't twist the copper line.
If a fitting still bubbles after tightening, replace the part or call a technician. (Pro only)
How long the gas lasts
Venture's figures for one hour at full flame, across many models (Manual):

A gallon of propane holds about 91,500 BTU (Manual), and a gallon weighs about 4.2 lb (General). So a full 30 lb cylinder holds about 7 gallons, roughly 650,000 BTU. Your furnace burning nonstop would empty one in about 22 hours. Venture warns that on a very cold, windy day the furnace alone can use most of a 30 lb cylinder.

Shore power comes in as 50 amp service on two 120 V legs. The converter turns it into 12 V for lights, the pump, the furnace fan, the fridge board and the slides, and charges a house battery you supply yourself.
electrical flow · 50 A shore power to 12 V loads
The map follows Venture's manual. Breaker labels, fuse assignments and wire routes vary by build, so fill in the circuit schedule below from your own panels. (Check unit)
Shore power (Manual, 2019 spec)
The cord is a Furrion detachable 50 amp cord, about 26 to 28 ft long, with four prongs: two hot, one neutral, one ground.
50 amp service is 240 V across the two legs, but nothing in the trailer runs on 240 V. Each leg feeds its own side of the panel.

The 2019 Venture manual describes a 50 A two-leg panel and shows branch protection examples including A/C circuits. The exact main-breaker arrangement, branch quantity and circuit amp ratings must be read from the installed panel and its schedule; a second A/C breaker may represent prep only.

Venture recommends against reducer adapters (50 to 30, or 30 to 15). With one, you can't run everything, and pulling more than it handles can melt it and start a fire. If you have no choice, run one big load at a time. A 30 amp hookup gives about 3,600 W. (General)
If you need an extension cord, use one of equal or heavier gauge and don't leave the spare length coiled.
Never plug into a household outlet or break the ground path.
Fireplaces (Manual, 2019 spec)

You have two electric fireplaces. Each is 120 V, about 5,000 BTU, and draws 1,500 W (12.5 amps). Turn on the master switch, then the power switch. Venture says two fireplaces require 50 amp service, and some trailers have a double-pole double-throw switch, often in the front cabinet, that makes you choose between a fireplace and the A/C. Check whether yours has one. (Check unit)
GFCI (Manual)

Test the GFCI outlet monthly while you're using the trailer. Press TEST, the RESET button pops out and that outlet and the ones after it lose power. Press RESET to restore it. A GFCI doesn't protect against short circuits or overloads. Breakers do that. Check pedestal polarity with a plug-in tester before you connect.
Converter and 12 V panel (Manual)
The converter, 12 V fuse panel and 120 V breakers share one load center with a brown plastic front and a small access door. On some 50 amp trailers the fuses and breakers are in a separate box.

Venture describes 6–14 branch fuse positions and, for its illustrated converter, two 40 A reverse-polarity protection fuses. Actual fuse count and reverse-polarity ratings depend on the installed converter model. Copy values from its label and manufacturer manual, never from a generic illustration.
The converter has a cooling fan that speeds up with load or heat. If the fan never runs, the converter can overheat and cut out.
Radios and some other parts have their own inline fuses on their harness.
House battery (Manual)
Venture doesn't supply one. Fit a deep-cycle battery. The breakaway switch and the slides need it.
Check it at least every 30 days. Keep terminals clean and top up flooded cells with distilled water only.
Full charge is 12.7 V. It's discharged at 10.5 V, and going lower damages the plates.

Venture’s manual calls for an automatic-reset breaker within approximately 18 inches of the house battery positive lead. A 30 A value is documented for one described circuit, not proof of this VIN’s installed part rating; read the stamped device and trace its circuit.
Breakers you'll want to find (Manual)

rows: Under the black cover by the battery disconnect

blocks.text: Battery disconnect (Manual)

The switch is on the front frame angle. Turn it off whenever you're not using 12 V, so nothing drains the battery. It may not cut every circuit, and the breakaway circuit may still be live. Check what stays powered on yours. (Check unit)
7-way connector (Manual)
Venture's trailer-side wire colors:

rows: 12 V feed from the tow vehicle

blocks.text: The junction box is on the front cross member. The brake circuit has no fuse or breaker. Clean the plug contacts when they corrode. The tow vehicle battery and the trailer battery are linked through the plug, so unplug when parked or fit a battery isolator in the tow vehicle to keep from draining both.
Solar and TV (Manual, 2019 spec)
Your trailer is prewired for Furrion solar. A 10 amp portable solar receptacle, Zamp or Furrion, may be on the rear wall or the front corner. The panel is aftermarket.

The roof antenna head is fixed and can't be raised or turned. A 12 V power supply inside, with a push button, powers its amplifier. If the picture doesn't change when you switch it on and off, check for 12 V at the roof cable.
Circuit schedule (Check unit)
Find each one by switching off a single breaker and seeing what stops. Leave the live panel interior to an electrician. (Pro only)

Each appliance has its own maker's manual in the trailer's information packet, and that manual wins over this section. Write each model number into the register in the Component Register, Spare Parts and Tools chapter so you can find the right one.
Furnace, 30,000 BTU (2019 spec, Manual)
It needs 12 V and propane. The burner is sealed, drawing air through the upper vent and exhausting through the lower one.
Air out the trailer if you notice any odd smell. Make sure there's propane and the cylinder valve is open.
Set the thermostat to HEAT, 5 to 8 degrees above room temperature.
The blower starts within 15 seconds and runs a 30 second purge.
The board sparks and opens the gas for a 7 second ignition try. It makes three tries, then locks out.
After a lockout, turn the thermostat to its lowest setting, wait one minute, then try again.
To shut it off, turn the thermostat to lowest or OFF. The blower runs about two more minutes to clear the heat.
It needs 10.5 to 13.5 V at the furnace. Below 10.5 V it shuts down.
Don't run it while towing.
Keep the outside vents clear and never fit screens over them. Never close every register, or the furnace can overheat and shut down.
Gas pressure and electrode adjustments are technician work. (Pro only)
Range and oven (Manual, 2019 spec)
It's a 17 in oven with three high-output top burners and a glass cover.
Top burners have no standing pilot. Light one at a time with the igniter or a long lighter.
After a refill, air in the line delays lighting, and the burner can light suddenly when gas arrives. Keep your face and hands back.
If a burner goes out, turn it off and wait five minutes before relighting. If you still smell gas, don't relight.
The oven has a pilot. Push and hold the knob 5 to 7 seconds while you light it, then release. The oven thermostat isn't adjustable.
Open a vent or window whenever you cook. Never use the range for heat. Keep the privacy curtain secured away from it.
Refrigerator, 8 cu ft (2019 spec, Manual)
Venture used several fridge brands. The manual's controls section covers Norcold N7 and N8 models ending in V or X. Check the label inside yours.
It needs 12 V at its control board, even on gas or 120 V.
Automatic models cool on 120 V whenever it's available, even with propane on.
On an X model, the snowflakes on the display show the setting. On a V model, you change temperature by moving the thermistor clip on the fins. Two or more fins to the left is colder.
An absorption fridge needs to be close to level. The manual says within one degree in one place and three degrees in another, so get it as level as you can.
It needs both vents clear: air in at the lower service door, hot air out at the roof or upper side vent.
If yours has two side vents, a 12 V fan starts when the upper fins reach 150 degrees F. Its 5 amp inline fuse is inside the lower vent door, up between the wall and the coils.
Close each door until it clicks. Test the seals by closing a dollar bill in the door on all four sides. You should feel a slight drag.
Before storage, defrost, clean and prop the doors.
Driving doesn't hurt its cooling.
Campfire Cafe outdoor kitchen (2019 spec, Manual)

The floorplan shows a refrigerator and a TV in the outdoor kitchen. In Venture's manual, outdoor fridges are 120 V compressor units, 1.6 or 3.2 cu ft, so they only run on shore power. Any two-burner cooktop connects with a quick-connect propane hose and has no pilot. The sink drains to a holding tank through a flexible hose, and the faucet can double as an outdoor shower. Level the trailer before cooking, keep the maker's clearances, and let the cooktop cool before you put it away.
Roof air conditioner, 15,000 BTU (2019 spec)

One 15,000 BTU unit is standard, with wiring prep for a second. Count what's actually on your roof and write the brand and model in the Component Register, Spare Parts and Tools chapter. Venture's manual says little about the A/C, so the service steps below are general practice. Follow the A/C maker's manual where it differs.

rows: Every 2 to 4 weeks in use, more often in dust
Remove the ceiling grille, wash the foam filter in warm soapy water, dry fully, refit.
Strong, even flow at each vent. Weak flow means a dirty filter or a duct problem.
After 15 minutes, supply air is usually 15 to 20 degrees F cooler than return air. Much less points to dirty coils or low refrigerant.
Power off. Remove the shroud, use an A/C coil cleaner and a soft brush, straighten fins with a fin comb.
Check condensate drains and roof gasket
Pour a cup of water in the base pan and see it drain outside. Look for a flattened gasket or water stains on the ceiling.
Technician only. Never add refrigerant yourself. (Pro only)

blocks.text: Switch off the A/C breaker before removing any cover. Don't stand on the shroud.
A roof A/C can only pull the cabin so far below outside temperature. Start it early, shade the windows and use the awning on hot days.
After turning it off, wait a couple of minutes before restarting.
Breaker trips, icing or water inside the ceiling mean stop and call a technician.
Heat and sand hit tires, propane, the fridge, the battery and every seal on this trailer. Most of the fixes happen before you leave, not at the roadside.
Tires and towing
Set pressure cold, after the trailer has sat three hours or more. Pressure rises as tires warm on the road, so never let air out of a hot tire. (Manual)
Under-inflation and overload are what overheat tires. Check pressure at every fuel stop, and feel the hubs with the back of your hand. (Manual, General)
Venture's original tires are rated 75 mph or more. Read your sidewalls and stay well under the rating in heat. (Manual, General)
Sun and long parking crack sidewalls. Judge tires by age and condition, not tread alone, and cover them when parked. (General)
Put pads under the tongue jack and stabilizers on hot asphalt. (General)
Propane

Cylinder pressure rises about 1.5 percent for every 10 degrees F. A cylinder filled in the cool can vent through its relief valve in hot sun. Fill only to 80 percent, preferably in the cooler part of the day. (Manual)
Keep the cover on and the cylinders shaded. A smell around them is a possible leak until proven otherwise. (Manual, General)
Refrigerator
Absorption fridges lose cooling in high heat. Keep the lower and upper vents clear of sand and nests. (Manual, General)
If yours has two side vents, check that the 12 V vent fan runs once the fins get hot, and that its 5 amp fuse is good. (Manual)
Keep it level, pre-chill food before loading, and open it as little as you can. (Manual, General)
A/C and power
Pre-cool on shore power, close blinds, use the awning for shade. (General)
Clean the A/C filter more often in dust. Rinse sand out of the condenser coil with the power off. (General)
Run the A/C on proper 50 amp service. Switch off the fireplaces. Watch the pedestal plug for heat or discoloring, and move if you find any. (Manual, General)
Battery
Heat speeds up water loss. Venture says check at least every 30 days. In summer heat, check flooded batteries every two to three weeks and keep the compartment ventilated. (Manual, General)
Roof, seals and slides
UV ages the SuperFlex roof membrane and its sealant faster. Inspect every spring and fall and after sandstorms, and wash off dust. (2019 spec, Manual, General)
Condition slide and window seals every few months. Clean slide tracks after dusty trips. (General)
Wax the fiberglass. Fading isn't covered by Venture's warranty. (Manual)
Dry the awning fabric before rolling it up. (General)
Moisture, even in the desert

Showers and cooking add moisture fast, and a cool A/C ceiling makes it condense. Open the bath roof vent about 1/2 in while showering and run the range hood fan while cooking. Mold from condensation isn't covered by warranty. (Manual)
People and pets
Never leave anyone, including pets, in a closed trailer in heat. A power cut in summer is a safety problem, so have a cooler place to go. (General)
Hot-weather check before a trip
☐ Tires checked cold, date codes acceptable
☐ Hub check planned at each stop
☐ Fridge vents clear, vent fan works (if fitted)
☐ A/C filter clean, coil free of sand
☐ Battery water topped up
☐ Cylinders shaded, not overfilled, valves closed for travel
☐ Drinking water on board
☐ Shade gear packed

chapters.title: UAE extreme heat and desert camping field guide

blocks.text: For prolonged high heat, sand, intense UV and hot pavement. Original factory US-market equipment is described as 120 V/60 Hz 50 A split-leg shore service. UAE 230 V/50 Hz infrastructure cannot be plugged directly into that RV service. An appropriately designed, protected conversion or supply solution requires a licensed specialist and confirmation of every connected appliance. Never assume a travel adapter or basic transformer makes the installation safe.
Before leaving for a hot-weather trip
1. Check trailer tire date codes, condition and cold pressures against the actual trailer placard and installed tire rating. Check wheel bearings, brakes, breakaway system and spare.
2. Inspect roofs, skylights, vents, slide seals, sealant transitions, awning fabric and plastic covers for UV cracking. Photograph suspicious seams.
3. Clean accessible air-conditioning return filters and inspect roof coil/shroud condition from a safe service position; verify roof A/C operation before departure.
4. Confirm refrigerator type and ventilation, start precooling early, test with an independent thermometer and load only chilled food.
5. Check battery terminals, temperature and charging profile; inspect heat-exposed cables and connectors for discoloration or brittleness.
6. Carry drinking water and an independent cooling/evacuation plan. Do not rely on the RV A/C as the sole heat safety system.
On-site cooling and electrical operation

rows: Park with sensible shade, close blinds, reduce door opening, clean filters and avoid unnecessary heat sources; expect a gradual temperature drop
If breaker trips, plug heats, compressor short-cycles or airflow fails, turn unit off and investigate
Use a professionally matched 120 V 60 Hz supply and energy budget; stagger startup of large loads
Do not energize factory 120 V appliances from an unverified UAE 230 V feed
Keep exterior vents unobstructed, shade fridge side without covering vents, minimize door opening, use thermometer
Move perishable food to reliable refrigeration if temperature becomes unsafe
Shade compartment as designed, keep required ventilation and check charger settings against chemistry
Swelling, gas odor, leaking or hot terminals: isolate safely and get service
Retract awning; close windows and roof vents where safe; keep combustion vents clear; protect water fittings
Never tape over A/C, furnace, fridge, water-heater or battery ventilation
Measure cold pressures before travel; inspect temperature differences across wheel positions as a warning, not a pressure target
Do not bleed hot tires down to placard cold PSI; stop for a markedly hotter hub or tire

chapters.title: How-to guides for factory trailer systems

blocks.text: Field procedures for the original 2019 STT343VBH configuration (VIN [VIN REDACTED]). These guides explain ordinary owner operation; they do not replace the exact instructions on the installed appliance, control board, or safety label. Read the applicable component label before using a switch. If your unit differs, stop and use the installed model’s manual.
Use the Trip Operations Checklists later in this workbook as the signed-off record; use these how-to pages whenever a checklist step is unfamiliar.
1 | LevelMatePRO: identify, connect, calibrate and use

Factory status: Venture lists LevelMatePRO as a mandatory 2019 SportTrek Touring feature. The factory OEM unit is powered from the RV 12 V system. Identify the actual module and its label before applying these steps. Some aftermarket LevelMatePRO models use coin cells and differ. The manufacturer’s OEM manual linked below is a later edition and must be checked against your installed module revision.
First-time phone connection and setup
1. Park safely, chock wheels and provide reliable 12 V battery power. Find the OEM LevelMatePRO control module and note its label/orientation; do not unmount or rotate it casually.

2. Install the official LevelMatePRO app on the phone; enable Bluetooth and any permissions required by the current phone operating system. Do not pair through the phone’s generic Bluetooth menu unless the specific app instructions require it.

3. For an OEM module with a front learn button, press and hold the button about three seconds until two beeps. The pairing window is approximately ten minutes. Open the app and follow its connection/registration prompts; repeat learn mode if the window expires.
4. Select Travel Trailer in the app’s setup wizard. For an installed OEM module, follow the OEM manual’s guidance to skip its portable-device signal-strength positioning test.

5. Measure the geometry the app asks for at its indicated points (wheel/axle spacing, left-to-right measurement, and any hitch reference). Enter measured values and units, not the trailer’s overall brochure length or body width.

6. Confirm module mounting orientation in the app. With a reliable independent level, bring the trailer truly level both ways, then use Set Level/calibration. Recheck the display against the physical level.
7. Practice connection, Disconnect/Sleep if available, and Set/Recall Hitch Position before the first trip. Screens and wording may vary by app and module firmware.

STOP / CHECK: If your module lacks the described learn button or beeps, do not force it. It may be the Venture Leveling System (VLS) variant or another revision; use the label-specific VLS/OEM manual. Never calibrate on an unlevel surface.
At a campsite: use LevelMatePRO correctly

1. While still coupled to the tow vehicle, open LevelMatePRO and check the side-to-side difference and which side is low. Estimate suitable leveling blocks under the wheels on the low side; use only blocks rated for the RV tire load.
2. Move slowly onto the blocks with a spotter. Stop, apply the tow vehicle parking brake, chock all trailer wheels securely, and verify the side-to-side result.
3. Unhitch using the proper hitch procedure; support the tongue jack foot. If you use the app’s Set Hitch Position, save it at the consistent coupler/ball reference described in the device manual.
4. Operate the power tongue jack to reach front-to-back level in the app. Independently check a countertop or floor with a reliable level.

5. Lower the four BAL electric stabilizers onto sound pads only to remove rocking. They are not leveling jacks and must not lift the frame or tires. Recheck LevelMatePRO and doors/slides before extending slides.

6. On departure, retract all stabilizers first. The Recall Hitch Position feature can help return the tongue to saved hitch height; still verify the ball, coupler, latch, chains, breakaway cable, 7-way plug and weight-distribution hitch visually.
Troubleshoot LevelMatePRO
1. No sensor seen: check RV 12 V supply, disconnect position, fuse and the module’s power indication; wake it or restart learn mode using the installed model’s instructions.

2. Connection times out: move near the module, enable Bluetooth/phone permissions, close conflicting sessions and repeat the OEM learn-button pairing window; one phone may need to disconnect before another connects.
3. Arrows or inches seem wrong: check sensor mounting orientation, measurement points/units, and actual trailer level. Re-run Set Level on a known-level trailer.
4. Hitch height not repeatable: confirm the hitch-position save was made at the correct coupler reference; terrain, jack-foot blocking and vehicle suspension change the final geometry.
5. After service or a remounted sensor: repeat orientation and level calibration. If readings remain inconsistent, contact LogicBlue with the module label and app version.

Official references: https://levelmate.com/pages/manuals  | OEM manual: https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0641/8402/5309/files/LevelMatePRO-OEM-2022-User-Manual-2nd-Generation.pdf?v=1653672312  | VLS variation: https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0641/8402/5309/files/KZ-VLS-User-Manual.pdf?v=1653672312
2 | Arrival: from site inspection to ready-to-camp
1. Walk the campsite first: check overhead clearance, grade, ground firmness, utility reach, and all slide/awning clearances.
2. Level side-to-side with rated wheel blocks while coupled; chock before releasing the coupler.
3. Support the tongue jack, unhitch, level front-to-back, and lower the four BAL stabilizers to ground contact only.
4. With pedestal breaker OFF, inspect/test the correct 50 A outlet and dry cord, connect fully, then energize; use the RV’s equipment and qualified assistance if pedestal wiring is suspect.
5. Attach a drinking-water hose and pressure regulator; inspect for leaks and purge air. Confirm that the water heater is full before energizing it.
6. Check slides’ exterior and interior paths, extend fully using the correct labeled switches, then set up the awning only if wind and weather permit.
7. Test smoke, CO and LP alarms; note emergency exit and fire extinguisher access. Record the campsite setup inspection in the workbook.
STOP / CHECK: Do not deploy stabilizers as lifting jacks, slide rooms while obstructed or severely unlevel, or connect to a damaged pedestal.
3 | Power tongue jack and BAL independent stabilizers
1. Before operating the tongue jack, chock wheels, inspect jack foot/blocking and keep hands away from the ram and coupler.
2. Use the tongue jack’s labeled Extend/Retract control in short intervals; stop at travel limits. Use LevelMatePRO for front-to-back level, not for estimating a safe jack load.
3. For four separate stabilizers, place solid pads at contact points. Run each motor only until the foot contacts and gently steadies the frame; alternate positions if needed.
4. Before towing, fully retract all four stabilizers and the tongue jack; secure any removable jack foot and verify road clearance.
STOP / CHECK: A strained motor, twisted foot, lifting tire, unusual chassis movement or repeatedly tripping breaker is a stop condition. Never crawl under a trailer supported only by jacks.
4 | Slide rooms: extend, retract and inspect
1. Level and stabilize first; maintain adequate 12 V supply for the drive controls.
2. Walk around all three slide travel zones and check trees, pedestals, furniture, cabinets, floor rugs, loose items and people.
3. Operate only the switch labeled for the desired room; hold it while watching and listening throughout travel. Stop immediately for binding or uneven motion.
4. Run to the normal full in/out stop according to that mechanism’s instructions, then release the switch. Verify bulb/wiper seals and no exposed gap.
5. Before departure retract every slide, confirm fully seated seals, clear locks or restraints if equipped, and visually inspect outside.
STOP / CHECK: Do not repeatedly reverse a stuck room, force it with vehicle movement, or use a generic manual override procedure. Identify the actual drive model before emergency retraction.
5 | Power patio awning
1. Check overhead/side clearance and current wind forecast; move chairs and people clear of the arm sweep.
2. Operate the labeled awning switch while watching both arms and fabric. Extend only as the installed model permits, with proper rain runoff slope if adjustable.
3. Retract immediately for increasing wind, storms, heavy rain, departure, or any period the awning is unattended.
4. Before travel verify the awning is fully nested, arms latched if provided, and fabric secure.
STOP / CHECK: An electric awning is a shade, not a storm shelter. Never assume automatic retract or wind sensing is installed.
6 | 50 A shore power, converter and GFCI
1. Turn off major RV loads. Inspect the cord, plug and pedestal for heat damage, water or broken covers; have an electrician test an uncertain pedestal.
2. With pedestal breaker OFF, connect the RV end and then the pedestal end fully; turn breaker ON and confirm normal 120 V operation.
3. Test the GFCI receptacle using TEST then RESET. Identify which outlets it protects. Check that the converter is maintaining the 12 V system.
4. When unplugging, switch off RV loads and pedestal breaker first. Remove plug by the body, protect connectors, and stow the cable clean and dry.

STOP / CHECK: Hot plugs, burning odor, tingling frame, repeated breaker trips or reversed-polarity/ground faults require immediate shutdown and qualified diagnosis. Do not defeat grounding or a breaker.
7 | Battery disconnect and 12 V distribution
1. Locate the labeled battery disconnect on the front frame and the 12 V fuse/breaker panel; photograph the installed labels for your component register.
2. For dry camping, begin with a fully charged battery and monitor state of charge under realistic loads. Keep the battery connected as required for critical safety-related systems.
3. If a 12 V device fails, reduce loads and inspect only the correctly identified same-rated fuse or resettable breaker; investigate repeat failures.
4. During storage, follow the battery manufacturer’s charging and isolation plan; some circuits can remain energized despite the main disconnect.
STOP / CHECK: Do not bypass a fuse, substitute a higher rating, or assume disconnecting 12 V disables the breakaway-brake circuit. Charging requirements depend on battery chemistry.
8 | Freshwater tank, city water and pump
1. Use a potable-water hose, clean fill fitting and documented tank-fill opening; never force an unknown valve. Fill slowly while watching vent/overflow and tank gauge.

2. For city water, attach a pressure regulator and filter if used, then pressurize gently. The 2019 guide identifies approximately 45 psi as a prudent regulated target; observe the installed component limits.
3. For onboard supply, fill the fresh tank, close fixtures and switch the water pump ON. Open a cold tap to purge air; check for cycling when faucets are closed.
4. Inspect the wet bay, under sinks, toilet and exterior connections for leaks before leaving the trailer unattended. Switch pump OFF for travel and extended absence.
STOP / CHECK: Continuous pump cycling usually means a leak, air entry or pressure-switch issue. Never leave a suspect pressurized system unattended.
9 | Six-gallon gas/electric water heater
1. Confirm the heater tank is full: open a hot faucet until a smooth stream appears, with the correct bypass valves in normal-use position.
2. Identify the actual gas and electric heater controls and the outside service compartment. Switch on only the desired energy mode after confirming the tank is full.
3. For propane ignition, listen for the normal ignition attempt and check the fault lamp where fitted. For electric, verify the installed element switch and shore-power capability.
4. To shut down, turn OFF gas/electric heater switches. Allow to cool before draining or opening the pressure relief valve.
STOP / CHECK: Never energize the electric element or fire the burner with an empty tank. Scalding water, propane odor, persistent ignition fault, soot, or leaking relief valve warrants shutdown.
10 | Holding tanks, toilet and black-tank flush
1. Use RV-approved toilet paper and adequate flush water; leave the black dump valve CLOSED during use so liquids do not drain away from solids.
2. At a dump station, wear gloves and connect the sewer hose securely. Drain BLACK first, then GRAY to help rinse the hose; close each valve when finished.

3. If a dedicated black-tank flush is equipped, use a separate clearly marked nonpotable hose, a backflow-protected water source and the precise flush-port warnings. Keep the dump valve open as instructed by the flush system; never leave it unattended.
4. Rinse and cap the hose, clean fittings, add the appropriate starting water to the black tank and log tank service.
STOP / CHECK: Never attach drinking-water gear to the black flush port, allow tank overpressure, or trust tank-level lights as exact measurements.
11 | Refrigerator and food-safe travel
1. Identify the installed refrigerator type and its controls; use its own model instructions for gas, 120 V or 12 V operating modes.
2. Level the trailer within the refrigerator maker’s operating limits, supply the required power/fuel, and start precooling well before loading perishable food.
3. Confirm safe food temperature with a separate refrigerator thermometer before loading. Keep door seals clear and exterior ventilation openings unobstructed.
4. Before towing, secure door latches and contents and use only travel modes expressly permitted by the appliance and local rules.
STOP / CHECK: Ammonia smell, yellow residue, soot, no cooling after correct setup, or a blocked exterior vent requires shutdown and inspection. Never run propane appliances where prohibited.
12 | Thermostat, roof air conditioning and furnace
1. Identify the thermostat’s mode/fan controls and which roof A/C unit it operates. Start with a moderate set point and ensure vents/returns are unobstructed.
2. On shore power, confirm the connected supply can carry the A/C startup load; wait through the thermostat’s compressor protection delay after changing modes.
3. For heat, confirm safe propane supply, charged 12 V battery and clear exterior furnace vents; select Heat and monitor the first ignition and warm-air flow.
4. Clean accessible return filters as instructed and record unusual cycling or fault indications before calling for service.
STOP / CHECK: Do not run furnace with blocked exterior combustion exhaust, store items against it, or attempt burner/gas-valve repair. Stop for CO alarm or combustion smell.
13 | Range, oven, microwave and fireplace
1. For range/oven, ventilate and follow the installed appliance’s lighting instructions exactly; never use cooking appliances for space heating.
2. Confirm microwave is secured, vented as designed and powered from a suitable circuit; avoid running several major 120 V loads on a limited hookup.
3. For electric fireplace, identify its heat setting and clearance requirements; keep bedding and furniture away from air inlets and outlets.
4. Turn all cooking and heating devices off before towing, fueling, tank service or departure.
STOP / CHECK: If you smell propane, avoid switches/flames, get everyone outside, close cylinder supply only if safe, and seek professional assistance.
14 | Campfire Café / exterior kitchen, if fitted
1. Confirm the exterior hatch is supported and every component is actually installed; 2019 features can differ by production and substitutions.
2. For any exterior stove or quick-connect, identify the approved propane connection and appliance pressure rating. Have a qualified technician confirm compatibility before first use.
3. Operate the outdoor refrigerator, sink and storage only within their installed manuals and keep the hatch clear of heat and water exposure.
4. Shut off fuel and power, cool appliances, secure fittings and latch the hatch before travel.
STOP / CHECK: Do not attach a high-pressure appliance to a low-pressure RV quick-connect or improvise adapters.
15 | Alarm checks and emergency isolation
1. Before each trip, test smoke, CO and LP-gas alarms with their TEST controls; check dates and replace units as their labels require.
2. Locate the fire extinguisher, emergency exits, propane cylinder shutoffs, shore breaker, battery disconnect and water pump switch; show every traveler.
3. For propane leak suspicion, evacuate and keep ignition sources off. For electrical smoke, disconnect safe upstream power without touching damaged wiring.
4. For water leaks, switch the pump OFF, stop city water and dry accessible areas. Document damage and seek repair before restarting systems.
STOP / CHECK: Treat an active CO alarm or suspected fire as an emergency. Get outside immediately and call emergency services; do not troubleshoot inside.
16 | Winterization and spring return to service

1. Use the full Winterizing chapter for your actual plumbing layout: drain tanks and low points, protect the heater using its exact bypass/drain instructions, and pump only RV-approved antifreeze where needed.
2. Label every changed bypass valve and drain plug position on your as-built diagram; never pump antifreeze into a water-heater tank when bypassed.
3. In spring, inspect for freeze damage, restore valves/plug, flush and sanitize potable lines as directed, and test under gentle water pressure before using the heater.
4. Recommission battery/12 V, LevelMatePRO, brakes, tires, seals, alarms, propane and appliances using the return-to-service checklist.
STOP / CHECK: Compressed-air pressure, antifreeze type and heater/anode details depend on installed component models. Do not guess at valves behind an enclosed panel.
17 | Hitching, brake check and departure
1. Confirm slide rooms, awning and stabilizers fully retracted, utility connections capped, roof fixtures closed, loose belongings secured and tanks/doors locked.
2. Chock wheels. Use LevelMatePRO Recall Hitch Position only as an aid to approximate coupler height; back tow vehicle in slowly with a spotter.
3. Lower coupler fully onto the correct-size ball, close and secure latch, attach rated safety chains crossed below the tongue, breakaway cable and the 7-way plug.
4. Set up and tension the weight-distribution hitch per its installed manual; raise tongue jack fully and remove all chocks only when ready to move.
5. Check running/stop/turn lights, controller connection, trailer brake operation at low speed, mirror view, tire pressure and load. Walk around the entire rig one last time.
STOP / CHECK: Do not depart if the hitch latch, breakaway function, brakes, lights, wheels/tires or load rating are in doubt. App hitch height is not a hitch-security check.
Owner equipment verification card

Fill in the component register before relying on model-specific recovery procedures: LevelMatePRO module revision and serial; slide drive brand/model (each room); BAL jack model and breaker labels; tongue jack rating; awning model; converter/charger and battery chemistry; 50 A panel/GFCI locations; water-heater model; furnace and A/C models; refrigerator; outdoor kitchen components. Photograph each rating plate and store it with the workbook.

Flames out. Everyone out. No switches.
Close cylinder valves if safe. Ventilate. Call a propane supplier or the fire department. (Manual)

Press Test/Mute, ventilate, don't go back in until it clears. See a doctor for headache, nausea or dizziness. (Manual, General)
Use the extinguisher only on a small fire with your exit behind you. (General)
Check the pedestal breaker, then the trailer main breakers, then the GFCI.
Reset each once. A repeat trip means unplug big loads and get help. (Manual)
Check the battery disconnect and the monitor panel battery light.
Check the battery breaker and fuses. Plug in shore power to charge. (Manual)
Water off at the pedestal, pump off.
Find and isolate the leak. Dry the area. (Manual, General)
Hold the wheel straight. Ease off the throttle.
Slow gradually, pull well off the road, hazards on, triangles out. (Manual, General)
Ease off the throttle. Don't brake hard.
Light pressure on the controller's manual lever, steer straight, then check load and hitch. (General)
Slow with the engine and lower gears.
Check the 7-way plug and controller. Don't drive on with a brake fault. (General)
Check battery, breaker and obstructions, then use the override for your slide system. (Manual)

blocks.text: Changing a tire at the roadside (Manual)
Pull completely off the road if you possibly can. Hazards on, flags or triangles out.
Chock the good tires.
Put blocking under the main frame rail, with the jack on top of it, in front of the spring hanger. Always on the main rail.
Break the lug nuts loose before lifting. Don't take them off yet.
Jack until the tire clears the ground.
Add more blocking under the frame. Never rely on the jack alone. Make sure the trailer is solid.
Remove the nuts and the wheel, fit the spare and snug the nuts.

Lower the wheel to the ground and torque the fasteners in the specified pattern to the installed wheel and axle manufacturer's value. The 2019 Venture general manual contains two different torque ranges, so verify the applicable value on the wheel decal or with the axle/wheel maker.

Re-check wheel torque at the intervals specified for your installed wheels. The general 2019 Venture manual mentions 50 and 200 miles in its lug section and 100 miles after a tire change; follow the applicable wheel/axle instructions.
The spare is mounted under the trailer on the 2019 Touring. Know how to drop it before you need to. (2019 spec)
Fire extinguisher, in short (General)
Pull the pin, aim at the base of the fire, squeeze, sweep side to side. Don't fight a propane fire unless the gas is off. Never go back in for belongings.
If the trailer comes off the hitch (Manual, General)

The breakaway switch should apply the trailer brakes from the house battery. Stop safely and keep people clear. Don't leave the pin out once the trailer is secure, because the brakes stay energized and can be damaged. Have the coupler, chains and hitch inspected before towing again.
Black tank overflow (General)
Close the termination valve and stop using the toilets and showers. Clean up with gloves and a disinfectant. Check the vents and hose for a blockage before using the system again.
Severe weather (General)
Retract the awning in wind. Bring the slides in if you might need to leave. Don't shelter in the trailer during a tornado warning or a severe sandstorm warning. Go to a solid building.

Mark where each shutoff is on your trailer, and photograph it.

blocks.text: Water heater fault light (General)

Many DSI water heaters have a small fault light by the gas switch. Owners report it lights during ignition and goes out once the burner catches. If it stays on, the heater has locked out. The usual causes are an empty cylinder, a closed valve, air in the line after a refill, or a failing board. Check your heater's own manual for its exact signals, since Venture's manual doesn't describe the light.
LevelMatePRO (General)

If readings seem wrong, confirm the correct LevelMatePRO OEM module is connected, the physical mounting orientation and measured wheelbase/track dimensions were entered correctly, and Set Level was calibrated on a genuinely level trailer. Verify against an independent spirit level. The factory-installed OEM system is powered by trailer 12 V: do not look for a seasonal coin-cell replacement unless an aftermarket battery-powered unit is actually fitted. See the detailed LevelMatePRO guide in the next chapter. (2019 Touring feature list; LogicBlue OEM manual)
Your fault log

These are jobs an owner can do safely with basic tools. Anything on propane, live 120 V wiring, brakes, bearings, the frame or a soft roof deck goes to a technician.
R1. Replace a 12 V blade fuse (Manual, General)
Switch off the load that stopped working.
Find its fuse in the load center (brown front, small door) and pull it with a fuse puller.
Check it. A broken strip or a dark window means it's blown.
Fit a fuse of exactly the same type and amp rating. Never a bigger one.
Switch the load back on once. If the new fuse blows, leave the circuit off and have the short traced.
R2. Reset a GFCI (Manual)
Unplug everything on that outlet group.
Check for water or damaged plugs and fix the cause first.
Press RESET on the GFCI outlet (or the GFCI breaker, on some trailers).
If it won't reset, or trips again with nothing plugged in, leave it off and call an electrician.
R3. Clean the water pump strainer (Manual)
Turn the pump off, disconnect city water and open a cold faucet to drop the pressure.
Put a towel and tray under the strainer on the pump's inlet side.
Unscrew the cup, rinse the screen, check the O-ring.
Refit by hand without cross-threading.
Turn the pump on and watch for drips before you close the compartment.
Venture says do this at least once a year. Some trailers hide the pump behind a screwed-on cover, which is there to protect the plumbing.
R4. Track down a water leak (Manual, General)
Water off at the pedestal, pump off, water heater off.
Dry what you can see. Lay paper towels under each fitting you can reach: sinks, toilets, pump, water heater, city inlet.
Turn on one water source briefly and watch the towels.
Venture's fittings are plastic or copper with compression rings. Snug a loose one gently. Plastic cracks if overtightened.
Shut off again the moment you see a drip. If the leak is inside a wall or floor, stop and book a repair before the structure gets wet.
R5. Touch up roof or seam sealant (2019 spec, Manual, General)
Venture expects sealants inspected every spring and fall. Your roof is SuperFlex one-piece membrane over walkable decking.
Work only on a dry day, on the decking, away from the edges. Use the ladder (200 lb limit).
Clean and dry the joint.
Use a sealant the roof maker approves for that membrane. Household silicone is the wrong product.
Remove loose failed sealant only where the maker allows. Apply over sound, dry material.
Let it cure fully, then water-test.
If the deck feels soft, the membrane is blistered or ceiling panels are stained, stop and get a specialist. (Pro only)
R6. Clean the A/C return filter (General)
Thermostat off and A/C breaker off.
Remove the ceiling grille and take out the foam filter.
Wash it in warm soapy water, rinse, and let it dry completely.
Refit and check airflow. Never open the rooftop unit while it's powered.
R7. Clean and inspect slide seals (Manual, General)
Bring the room in and switch off the slide breaker.
Brush grit off the bulb and wiper seals. Wash with mild soap and water and dry.
Treat with a rubber conditioner made for RV seals.
Photograph splits, flat spots and gaps at the corners. Note the seal profile before ordering a replacement.
Don't touch stops, gears, cables or timing without the slide maker's manual.
R8. Grease the E-Z Lube hubs (Manual)
Remove the rubber cap from the axle end.

Do not apply a fixed number of grease-gun strokes to an unidentified hub. Follow the installed axle manufacturer's E-Z Lube procedure, or have a qualified technician perform service. Check brakes for grease contamination.
Wipe off excess and refit the cap.
This tops up grease. It doesn't replace bearing and seal inspection or repacking, which is shop work. (Pro only)
R9. Clean the 7-way plug and battery terminals (Manual, General)
Unplug the 7-way. For the battery, turn off the disconnect and remove the negative cable first.
Clean corrosion with a small brush. A baking soda and water paste neutralizes battery acid.
Dry, then coat plug contacts with dielectric grease.
Reconnect the battery positive first, negative last.
R10. Fix a loose cabinet latch or hinge (General)
Match the original part's size and screw holes. Use short screws so you don't hit wiring or pipes behind the panel. Don't overtighten into thin cabinet panels.

blocks.text: Running the twice-a-year inspection

In spring, do every spring and yearly row, then recommission (the Winterizing, Storage and Return to Service chapter). In fall, do the fall rows, then store or winterize. Write each pass in the service log in the Logs chapter and photograph anything that changed since last time, so you can compare.

chapters.title: Winterizing, storage and return to service

blocks.text: Winterize only if the trailer will see freezing temperatures. For long hot-weather parking, the storage steps matter more than antifreeze. Venture doesn't cover freeze damage.
Winterizing, Venture's two methods (Manual)
Drain and flush the holding tanks first, then drain the fresh system as in the Fresh Water, Water Heater and Plumbing chapter.
Method 1, compressed air
Open all faucets, low-point drains, the toilet valve and the water heater drain, and leave them open.
Run the pump 20 to 30 seconds until it's dry.
Connect an air hose to the city water inlet with an adapter and blow the lines out for 3 to 5 minutes.
Pour 1 pint of RV antifreeze into each sink and tub drain to protect the P-traps.
Venture doesn't give an air pressure limit. Many technicians keep it low, around 40 psi or under. Check your plumbing and water heater makers' limits before you start. (General)
Method 2, bypass and RV antifreeze
Turn the pump switch off.
Drain the water heater and the whole water system.
Turn both bypass valves so their handles are vertical. That takes the water heater out of the system.
Open all faucets.
Put the siphon hose in a container of RV antifreeze.
System 1: close V2, open V1. System 2: close V3, open V2 and V1.
Turn the pump on. Close each faucet, hot and cold, when antifreeze comes out. Include the outside shower and the toilet.
The pump shuts off at about 40 psi once the lines are full. Turn it off and release the pressure.
Pour 1 pint of antifreeze into each drain for the P-traps.

Use only non-toxic RV antifreeze. Never automotive (ethylene glycol) or windshield washer antifreeze. Venture keeps antifreeze out of the water heater because it would take 6 to 10 more gallons, attacks the anode rod and leaves sediment. If you winterize without the bypass, take the anode out and fit a 3/4 in drain plug. Don't drink water that has had any antifreeze in it. Label the trailer as winterized.
Also drain or protect the outdoor kitchen faucet and any water filter housing. (General)
Parking for weeks or months (Manual, General)
Park on firm, level ground. Chock the wheels. The stabilizers only steady the trailer.
Set tires to placard pressure and cover them against sun. Move the trailer a little every few weeks to change the contact patch. (General)
Turn off the battery disconnect. Charge the battery fully first, and recharge it at least monthly. (Manual, General)
Leave the breakaway pin in. Pulling it in storage corrodes the switch. (Manual)
Close both cylinder valves and fit the dust caps. Keep the cylinders outside the trailer. (Manual)
Empty and clean the fridge, defrost it, and prop the doors slightly open. (Manual)
Dump and rinse both holding tanks. Leave the valves closed.
Take out food and anything that draws pests. Seal gaps where pipes pass through the floor, but never block the furnace, water heater or fridge vents. (Manual, General)
Open cabinets and closets a crack for air. Use moisture absorbers. Check monthly for leaks, mold, pests and flat tires. (Manual, General)
Run the A/C on fan for 15 to 20 minutes before closing up to dry the coil, then clean the filter. (General)
Retract all three slides and the awning. Condition seals first. Use a breathable cover if you use one. (General)

For the factory OEM LevelMatePRO, follow the OEM sleep/power instructions and maintain the trailer battery appropriately; it has no routine coin-cell removal. If a different aftermarket sensor is fitted, follow its labeled manual. (LogicBlue OEM manual)
Return to service, in this order
Walk around. Roof, seams, slide seals, tires, lights, underbelly. Look for leaks, pests and damage.

Tires and wheels: verify cold inflation from the tire placard and lug torque from the installed wheel and axle documentation. Venture's general 2019 manual gives conflicting torque ranges in different sections, so use the component specification and wheel decal. Have bearings and brakes serviced as required.

Battery. Reconnect and charge; check electrolyte only if the installed battery is serviceable. Restore 12 V power and reconnect the factory OEM LevelMatePRO in its app. Do not install a coin cell in an OEM hard-wired sensor.
Shore power. Test the pedestal, inspect the cord, test the GFCI, confirm the converter fan runs. (Manual)
Propane. Fit cylinders, open slowly, leak-test every connection, light a burner to purge air. (Manual)

Water. Set the bypass handles horizontal. Fill the tank. Flush antifreeze from every faucet, the toilets and the outside shower. Sanitize (the Fresh Water, Water Heater and Plumbing chapter). Check for leaks with the pump running.
Water heater. Confirm it's full, then test gas and electric separately, not together. (Manual)
Appliances. Furnace (watch the purge and ignition), range and oven, fridge on 120 V and gas, fireplaces, A/C.
Slides, jacks and steps. Run each slide with a helper watching. Run the stabilizers and tongue jack.
Alarms. Test smoke and CO/propane alarms and check their dates. (Manual)
Towing gear. Lights, brake controller, breakaway battery and pin.
Shakedown. A short local drive. Stop after about 10 miles and check hubs, hitch and lug nuts. (General)
Log it in the Logs chapter.

After a year or more parked, add a shop inspection of bearings and brakes, replace tires past your age limit even if the tread looks good, and check the propane hoses, roof sealant and slide seals, since rubber ages in storage. (General)

How to identify a circuit safely
1. Photograph the closed load center and all labels. Identify make/model, fuse-board slot numbers and the actual number of breaker poles.
2. Copy the printed amp rating and circuit label for each position without touching conductors. Mark discrepancies between the door chart and installed protection.

Look at the ceiling. A row of small vents along the ceiling, fed from the roof unit, means a ducted system. One ceiling box under the roof unit with its own louvers and filter means a direct, non-ducted unit. Ducted systems need their joints checked for leaks. Direct units only need the filter and the ceiling box gasket checked.
